items.bold: TRUMP PAUSED PROJECT FREEDOM — "Mutually agreed — paused to see if Agreement can be finalised." One-page MOU close.
items.text: Business Standard (2hr ago) and BusinessToday confirmed: Trump posted on Truth Social Wednesday: "We have mutually agreed that, while the Blockade will remain in full force and effect, Project Freedom will be paused for a short period of time to see whether or not the Agreement can be finalized and signed." Separately, BusinessToday reported that US and Iran are reportedly close to a one-page memorandum of understanding (MOU) that could pave the way to end the war. Sources say this is the closest the parties have been to an agreement since the war began February 28. The US is seeking an Iranian response on several key points within the next 48 hours, though no agreement has been reached yet. The Project Freedom pause is the most positive diplomatic signal since Trump said "concept of deal" on Saturday — but this time with an operational concession: Project Freedom is actually stopped.

items.bold: BRENT PLUNGED 8.44% to $100.60 — largest single-day fall since March ceasefire. WTI also tumbled.
items.text: Business Standard Capital Markets confirmed: Brent crude for July 2026 settlement slumped $9.27 or 8.44% to $100.60 per barrel on Wednesday. WTI also fell sharply. This is the largest single-day oil price decline since the March ceasefire rally. Markets are pricing a significant probability that the one-page MOU gets signed within 48 hours. CNBC Tuesday confirmed Brent had closed at $109.87 (-4%) Tuesday after Hegseth confirmed ceasefire not over — making the two-day Brent move from Tuesday open ($114+) to Wednesday close ($100.60) an extraordinary $13+ decline in two sessions. Even at $100.60, Brent remains 55% above pre-war ($65). The market is not pricing a full deal — just a high probability of a framework being agreed.

items.text: Business Standard confirmed: China told Iran a "comprehensive" ceasefire is needed as the war drags on — China's most direct intervention into the US-Iran negotiation yet. assessment.body:
Wednesday 6:45 PM IST. Day 68. The most significant diplomatic day of the West Asia War.

THE TUESDAY RECAP
• Hegseth: "ceasefire is not over" — full war not resuming
• Caine: Iran attacked US 10+ times since ceasefire — "below threshold"
• Brent closed $109.87 (-4%). Sensex -0.3% to ~77,018
• BJP landslide win in West Bengal — political stability confirmed
• M&M +3.4% on profit beat — domestic demand resilient
• Goldman Sachs specifically named India at risk of refined product scarcity

THE WEDNESDAY GAME-CHANGER
• Trump paused Project Freedom: "mutually agreed, paused to see if Agreement can be finalised"
• US-Iran close to a one-page MOU (BusinessToday sources)
• Closest to agreement since February 28
• US expects Iranian response on key points within 48 hours
• Brent plunged 8.44% to $100.60 — largest one-day fall since March ceasefire
• Sensex +941. Nifty topped 24,300. Rupee ~94. S&P 500 record 7,259

THE 48-HOUR CLOCK
• US expects Iranian response by Thursday-Friday
• Iran: "will only accept fair and comprehensive agreement"
• Nuclear enrichment recognition remains the core gap
• China told Iran "comprehensive ceasefire needed" — crucial external pressure
• If Iran accepts: MOU signed, Brent $80-88, Sensex +1,500-2,000 possible
• If Iran rejects: Project Freedom resumes, Brent back to $108+

INDIA's POSITION AT DAY 68
• Sensex +941. Nifty 24,300+. Rupee ~94
• ECLGS 5.0 approved — aviation and MSME war relief
• Three Indians wounded in Fujairah (May 5) — India in conflict narrative
• Goldman Sachs: India at specific risk of LPG and jet fuel scarcity
• Kharif fertiliser: still at risk even with MOU (months to normalise)
• BJP Bengal landslide = political stability premium

VERDICT: Day 68 is the most hopeful day of the entire West Asia War. Trump paused a military operation to create space for a deal. A one-page MOU is reportedly being negotiated. Brent crashed 8.44%. Global markets surged to records. The 48-hour clock is running on Iran. The question is whether Iran's Supreme Leader will authorise Araghchi to sign a framework that defers nuclear discussions — or whether Qalibaf's "new equation" hardline prevails. India wakes up Thursday watching one of the most consequential 48 hours since February 28.

featured.title: Geopolitics of LPG Supply in India
featured.desc: How India's LPG import dependency on the Gulf creates acute vulnerability during the West Asia War. Explores Hormuz exposure, alternative supply routes, and policy imperatives for energy security in a blockade scenario.

featured.desc: India imports 30%+ of its fertilisers via the Strait of Hormuz. This paper maps the supply chain risks to kharif and rabi crops, the strategic case for diversification, and what a prolonged blockade means for food security.
